observations:
Torah #132 is a self-contained two-sentence teaching that presents one and only one bechina equation: the tzaddik IS the spring (מעיין). All sub-concepts (the tzaddik's fame, the tzaddik's hiddenness, the hidden nourishment of tree roots) are aspects of this single metaphor, not independent bechina domains. They all belong to Package 1 (הצדיק והמעיין).

No new independent package is warranted for the following reasons:

1. SINGLE CONCEPTUAL DOMAIN: The entire teaching operates within one metaphorical domain — tzaddik-as-spring. There is no second domain, no second metaphor, no second bechina family. The teaching's three sub-aspects (visible appearance, underground hiddenness, underground nourishment) are facets of the same single equivalence.

2. NO EVIL MIRROR: The teaching contains no mention of a sitra achra, no opposing force, and no evil counterpart to the tzaddik/spring. A second (evil) package would require the presence of opposing concepts, which this brief text does not contain.

3. NO SECOND POSITIVE DOMAIN: Some Torahs identify multiple positive domains that are distinct enough to warrant separate packages (e.g., Torah #3's holy-music package vs. its night-Torah package vs. its chesed-protection package). Torah #132 has none of this complexity. There is no second spiritual domain, no secondary subject, no secondary metaphor that forms an independent bechina family.

4. שרשי אילנא AS EMBEDDED CONCEPT: One might consider whether שרשי אילנא (the tree roots) could anchor an independent package (e.g., connecting to the rich אילן/Abraham/chesed complex found in Torah #3 or elsewhere). However, in Torah #132 the tree roots appear only as the recipient of the spring's nourishment — they are the endpoint of the metaphor, not a developed bechina node with their own cluster. They function within Package 1 as the image of 'those spiritually rooted in the tzaddik' and do not form an independent package.

Conclusion: The single package identified — Package 1: הַצַּדִּיק וְהַמַּעְיָן (The Tzaddik and the Spring) — fully captures all bechina-connected conceptual content in Torah #132. No additional independent bechina domain exists in this teaching that would meet the threshold for a new package.
